what_its_for: Dolutegravir is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children. It belongs to a group of medicines called integrase inhibitors. It helps lower the amount of HIV in your blood, which helps your immune system work better and lowers your risk of getting HIV-related infections. This medicine does NOT cure HIV, but it helps control it.
how_to_take: Take dolutegravir by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. However, if you have certain drug-resistant HIV or if your doctor tells you to take it twice daily, take it with food to help it work better. Swallow the tablet whole. If you use the dispersible tablet (Tivicay PD), place it in a small amount of water (about 5 mL or 1 teaspoon), let it dissolve, and drink it right away. Do not chew or crush regular tablets. Always take it at the same time(s) each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 50 mg once a day. Some people may need 50 mg twice a day, such as those with certain resistant HIV strains or those taking certain other medicines. For children, the dose depends on their weight and age, so follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 20 hours since your scheduled time, take your missed dose as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 20 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can allow HIV to multiply and may make the medicine less effective over time.
storage: Store dolutegravir at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed and keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package. If you need to dispose of leftover medicine, ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, or laxatives containing magnesium or aluminum within 2 hours BEFORE or 6 hours AFTER taking dolutegravir, as these can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed into your body. Avoid taking it with certain other medicines like rifampin, St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), or metformin (a diabetes medicine) without talking to your doctor first. Always tell ALL your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine, vitamin, supplement, and herbal product you take to avoid harmful interactions. Do not share your medicine with others, and do not miss doses.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a rash with fever, blisters, peeling skin, or sores in your mouth or eyes (signs of a serious allergic reaction); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain (signs of liver problems); unusual muscle pain, weakness, or trouble breathing; feelings of sadness, depression, thoughts of harming yourself, or mood changes; signs of infection like fever, chills, or swollen glands (your immune system waking up, called immune reconstitution syndrome). Also tell your doctor if you become pregnant or are planning to become pregnant, as dolutegravir use in early pregnancy requires a careful discussion about risks and benefits.
when_it_works: Dolutegravir starts working right away, but you may not feel any different at first. After a few weeks of treatment, blood tests should show that the amount of HIV in your blood (called your viral load) is going down. Most people reach an undetectable viral load within 3 to 6 months of starting treatment. It is very important to keep taking your medicine every day, even when you feel well, because stopping can allow the virus to come back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking dolutegravir if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. There is a small risk of a certain type of birth defect (neural tube defect) when dolutegravir is taken at the time of conception. Your doctor will help weigh the benefits and risks with you. Take folic acid (a B vitamin) as directed. Breastfeeding: Dolutegravir passes into breast milk. In some countries, breastfeeding while on HIV treatment may be recommended with guidance; however, in countries where safe formula is available, it is generally advised NOT to breastfeed to avoid passing HIV to the baby. Ask your doctor for guidance. Kidney or Liver Disease: Dolutegravir can generally be used in mild-to-moderate kidney or liver disease, but your doctor may monitor you more closely. It is usually NOT recommended in severe liver disease. Elderly Patients: Older adults can take dolutegravir, but may need closer monitoring. Children: Dolutegravir can be used in children as young as 4 weeks old (or at least 3 kg) using the dispersible tablet form, with doses based on weight.
